item.title: Storage

item.title: Data Layout
item.description:
Underlying Question:

How to speed up the system by improving its data throughput

Learning Objectives:

  1. Data Layouts
  2. Row, Column, Hybrid
  3. Compression
  4. Bitlists, Approximations etc

What are the principal mapping steps to map a relation to a device?

1a. linearize:

To dimensional relations are mapped to a one dimensional sequence of values

1b. serialize:

a one dimensional sequence of values is ampped to bytes on virtual pages

2. devirtualize:

virtual pages are mapped to physical pages

item.title: Storage and Indexing
item.description:
Cost Model:

We will use the following notations and assumptions in our analysis:

BB is the number of data pages

RR is the nnumber of records per page

DD is the time required to read/write one page

CC is the time to process a record

The cost of I/O to dominates all other cost of a database opearations. Thus we use the number of page I/O’s as out cost metric.

item.title: Query Processing and Optimization
item.description:
Underlying Question:

How to compute complex queries at scale?

Learning Objective:

query optimization, query processing, operator models, pull, push, vectorization, rule vs cost; intra- vs inter-query parallelization , accross threads vs machines; mutable.

Computing the results of a query:

We have two options

  1. Brute Force (Scan): we inspect each and every tuple and check whether the query predicate holds for that tuple and add it to the result set.
  2. Index (Index Scan): We organixe the contents of the realation such that we do not have to inspect each and every tuple to determine whether the tuple belongs to the result set.

Partitioning Function:

Given a domain D, any function p: [R] → D is called a partitioning function.

item.title: Crash Recovery
item.description:
Underlying Question:

How do we make a system robust against software and hardware crashes

Learning Objective:

crash recover: failover, hot standby, loging, redo, undo, ARIES, elasticity

Introduction:

What is recovery?

By recovery we meant hat we can get back to a consistent state of the database according to the ACID properties.

What is the impact of failures on ACID?

Error scenarios affect the ataomicity i.e. only a part of the transaction is executed, and durability, i.e. only some of the actions of a transaction were made durable. These problems then affect the consistency of the database
